quotes.text: Accounts receivable tracks the money customers owe you along with the payments that come back. Think of it as a filing cabinet for the money inside of your business.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A one-sentence definition with a memorable analogy that frames the whole episode.

quotes.text: A contact list helps you call someone. A customer account records the financial relationship, including the rules that control what happens when the company sells to them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates a customer account from a simple contact record.

quotes.text: This matters because a payment without settlement can leave an open invoice sitting on the account, even though you already received the cash.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in plain terms why settlement is a necessary step after a payment arrives.

quotes.text: Many people hear credit management and assume it means turning customers away. It doesn't. It means agreeing on safe boundaries before a late payment becomes a much larger problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects a common misconception about the purpose of credit management.

quotes.text: An aging report shows what has already happened, but a prediction helps the team decide where to focus before the next late payment creates a problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Contrasts backward-looking aging reports with forward-looking payment predictions.

takeaways: Accounts receivable in Dynamics 365 Finance tracks what customers owe from the first invoice until the balance closes, using the rules stored on the customer account.
A payment only closes an invoice once it is settled against it; partial payments, payment reconciliation journals and centralized payments keep the open balance accurate.
Credit holds, collection lists, promises to pay, disputes and aging reports help finance and sales act on risk early without treating customers as case numbers.
hook: You made the sale and sent the invoice, but when does the money actually arrive, and what happens if it doesn't? This plain-English episode is for finance teams, consultants and business users who want to understand Dynamics 365 Accounts Receivable. Follow one customer balance from invoice to payment, credit checks and collections.
